original_prompt:
Play Atari Asterix. Collect useful objects and avoid lyres. Return only one integer: 0=NOOP, 1=UP, 2=RIGHT, 3=LEFT, 4=DOWN, 5=UPRIGHT, 6=UPLEFT, 7=DOWNRIGHT, 8=DOWNLEFT.
The game advances continuously at 6 raw frames per wall-clock second, 10 times slower than normal 60 FPS. Images are chronological; use their frame timestamps. The supplied history spans up to 32 raw frames, with the middle image 8 raw frames old and the newest image current. At most eight requests are in flight; observations are dropped when all workers are busy. A command becomes available only after your complete API response arrives. The newest completed observation wins and stale commands are discarded. UP/DOWN lasts at most four raw frames, then releases; LEFT/RIGHT continues. Further vertical commands based on observations before that hop finished have their vertical component ignored. Wait for a fresh observation before requesting another row change. The game continues to advance while your API response is computed. Do not use tools, explain, or analyze aloud. Output the action integer immediately.
Measured API complete-response delay: mean 1224 ms, median 1201 ms, P95 1841 ms. The actual delay of your request is unknown.
The player is yellow; white score popups are not targets. Objects move horizontally; UP/DOWN changes rows. Anticipate motion during the response delay and current held action. Intercept nearby safe collectibles, avoid lyres. Once aligned, release vertical motion. Use recent applied actions to maintain a maneuver unless a new hazard requires changing it.
